accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:switch-record-provenance, ass:metadata-timing, and thm:robust-design-complexity
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The logged switch record and its guard map are externally supplied protocol primitives; neither latent-edge realization nor the completion is inferred from acquired laws.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All identification and complexity claims are conditional on one ex ante selected source being evaluated after release of a genuine exogenous record h whose known guard map fixes G_h.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: GID is presented as a sound and complete fixed-graph procedure for identification from an arbitrary collection of experimental distributions, with thicket-based failure analysis.
Under positivity, a single c-component Q[S] is g-identifiable iff it is identifiable from one available source graph containing S, and the proposed algorithm is sound and complete.
The paper studies minimum-cost intervention design on a known ADMG, reduces its single-district form to hedge hitting, and proves its minimum-cost problem NP-complete.

source_verification_receipts.locator: publisher abstract and stated Section 4 / Theorem 1.3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published article states that Separating by Forbidden Pairs is Sigma_2^P-complete even on acyclic graphs; its public full theorem text was inaccessible.
The paper studies fixed-graph minimum-cost proxy experiment design and gives weighted Max-SAT and ILP reformulations plus an adjustment-design method.
The paper optimizes for the most plausible identifiable subgraph under probabilistic edge uncertainty and calls its NP-complete optimization problem edge-ID.
The paper establishes a broad abstract route to Sigma_2^P-complete minimum-cardinality interdiction/blocking problems, but does not provide the proposal's causal source semantics.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Prove a sharp tractability contrast for an explicitly defined weaker guard class, such as independent or monotone switches, so the field contribution isolates correlation rather than merely exhibiting a quantified-hard language.

Advance the bounded-terminal frontier by either a fixed-d splitter hardness construction or a boundary-signature FPT algorithm; either resolution would turn the current field kernel into a materially stronger complexity result.

Add a concrete protocol-level example whose logged mode bits plausibly alter specified confounding channels, together with a worked h-indexed source and certificate, to make the novel provenance assumption empirically legible.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the fixed-fiber protocol caveat retained; prioritize a correlation-versus-monotone-switch boundary theorem if the project seeks a higher tier.
